reason: E1 shows that high strain rate sliding in UHV on a coarse-grained HEA produces ultrafine grains and low friction, supporting the dynamic refinement premise. E2 provides a calculated high grain-boundary energy and notes that decohesion can occur without segregation, directly supporting the premises of reduced cohesion and segregation-free embrittlement. However, neither passage provides evidence that the refined grains are below a critical size for dislocation inhibition or that grain-boundary sliding becomes dominant, leaving those mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: High strain rate sliding in UHV induces dynamic grain refinement to ultrafine/nanocrystalline sizes in the HEA
Below a critical grain size, dislocation plasticity is inhibited and grain boundary sliding becomes dominant
Ultrafine high-angle grain boundaries in this HEA have reduced cohesive strength
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion leads to intergranular cavitation/decohesion and toughness degradation
This embrittlement occurs without conventional segregation or intermetallic precipitation
